requirements.requirement: Create the opsbot identity on node1 and the corresponding remote identity and SSH credentials needed on node2.
requirements.summary: opsbot exists as UID 1001 on both nodes with locked passwords and securely permissioned SSH directories. Node1 holds the 3072-bit RSA private key, and the matching public-key fingerprint is installed in authorized_keys on both systems.

requirements.requirement: Allow node1 to run commands on node2 over SSH as opsbot using a key.
requirements.summary: A direct node1-to-node2 public-key SSH session executed as opsbot on node2 successfully before the restarts and again after both nodes restarted.

requirements.requirement: Require key-based authentication for opsbot on both systems.
requirements.summary: The effective per-user sshd configuration on both nodes enables public keys, disables passwords, and requires the publickey method. Password-only connections to both systems were rejected before and after restart, while key-based logins succeeded.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 7.9 with kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64. The implementation used the platform's existing OpenSSH tools, and no package or OS/kernel replacement is evidenced.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for both nodes: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, independently corroborated changed boot identities, recovered sshd/account/key state, and successful post-restart node1-to-node2 operation were captured.
limitations: Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution on both nodes, so package-manager consistency could not be independently compared.
The retained reboot log files were inventoried, but their contents were not captured; their observed paths and creating commands are sufficient to identify the cleanup residue.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive account, key, sshd, known-host, reload, and restart mutations have clear roles in implementing, validating, or satisfying the mandatory restart protocol. Both restart commands unnecessarily left their bounded nohup output files in /tmp: /tmp/opsbot-reboot-node1.log and /tmp/opsbot-reboot-node2.log. These low-risk artifacts remained after execution and were not cleaned up. No failed services, new listening sockets, unsafe exposure, or other unexplained persistent changes were observed.
